title: Client-led checkpoint protocol for SSE multiplex proxies
text:
Client-led checkpoint protocol for SSE multiplex proxies

description:
Problem statement: Clients behind multiplexing proxies (API gateways, sidecars) observe opaque reconnect behavior when network hiccups or backend failovers occur. Current resume tokens are purely server-driven which leads to mismatches in client-owned request ordering, backpressure windows, and partial-function-call atomicity. This ticket proposes a client-led checkpoint protocol layered on top of the existing SSE framing to make reconnect deterministic for multiplexed streams and allow gateways to perform efficient reconnection and replay without losing function-call boundaries or violating backpressure SLOs.

Goals: Create a lightweight, backward-compatible protocol extension that: 1) lets clients request or declare checkpoints tied to logical stream lanes; 2) encodes minimal checkpoint metadata in a length-prefixed control event; 3) enables proxies to hold and replay fragments for a short grace window; 4) preserves tool/function-call atomicity across reconnects; and 5) surfaces telemetry and hints to the Console for observability.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change chunk encoding for payloads, introduce persistent server-side long-term storage for replays, or require TLS-level renegotiation. It should be deployable as an opt-in feature flag for gateways and clients.

acceptance_criteria:
Define a control-event format that fits into existing SSE event lines and is ignored by legacy clients
Proxy shim can accept a client-declared checkpoint and retain fragment window for the configured grace period
On reconnect the client can request resume using the checkpoint id and receive deterministic continuation that maintains function-call boundaries
Console shows per-checkpoint telemetry (duration, bytes replayed, success/fallthrough) for instrumented requests
End-to-end test coverage demonstrating reconnection with interleaved function calls that remain atomic after replay

technical_notes:
Control event is an SSE event with event: checkpoint and data: length-prefixed base64 JSON. JSON fields: lane_id, checkpoint_id, last_complete_seq, backpressure_window_hint, timestamp_iso
Use base64 JSON to avoid newline/escaping fragility in existing SSE parsers and to keep event payload compact
Proxy behavior: on checkpoint declare, persist in-memory fragment buffer per lane for grace_window (configurable default 30s) and track bytes/seq; grace_window evicted if storage or memory pressure triggers LRU
On reconnect: client sends resume request as POST /v1/stream/resume with checkpoint_id (opaque) and optional prefer_delta boolean; server mediates replay or fallback to new stream depending on available fragments
Function-call atomicity: checkpoint must reference last_complete_seq which corresponds to the last tool call confirmed to have completed; replaying will resume only at subsequent tokens to avoid double-invoke semantics
Backpressure negotiation: clients include backpressure_window_hint in checkpoint; proxies expose a header to backend to allow short-term adjusted batch sizes on replay to avoid overcommitting GPU slots
Compatibility: Legacy clients will ignore unknown events; Gateways enable protocol via labeled annotation or header to avoid accidental adoption
Telemetry: emit structured logs when checkpoint created, buffer retained, replay attempted, and replay served; map to Console metrics and trace spans

tradeoffs_and_risks:
Memory footprint on proxies — in-memory buffering simplifies latency but increases RAM requirements; mitigated via configurable grace_window and per-lane size limits
Increased complexity for proxies and resume endpoint — adds surface area for bugs; mitigate with integration tests and a feature flag rollout
Potential semantic mismatch if clients checkpoint mid-toolcall — acceptance criteria enforce checkpoint semantics referencing last_complete_seq to avoid double-invoke
Replay may increase backend load during mass reconnect events — plan to rate-limit replays and fallback to fresh streams when pressure exceeds threshold

implementation_plan:
1) Design and spec: finalize control-event JSON schema and binary encoding (this ticket)
2) Proxy shim: implement in gateway codepath (retain buffer, expose resume endpoint, integrate LRU eviction)
3) Server/runtime: implement resume endpoint to validate checkpoint id, serve buffered fragments, or signal fallback
4) Client SDK updates: expose checkpoint() and resume() primitives; default to no-op on older SDKs
5) Console: add checkpoint telemetry panels and a replay-rate chart
6) End-to-end tests and chaos scenarios (network partition, proxy restarts, memory pressure)

testing_plan:
Unit tests for encoding/decoding of checkpoint control event
Integration tests where proxy holds fragments and a client reconnects requesting resume — verify token continuity and function-call atomicity
Load test where 1k clients simultaneously declare checkpoints and 200 reconnects per second to validate memory eviction behavior
Chaos test: restart proxy during grace_window and ensure clients gracefully fallback to fresh stream with no double-invocation
Observability test: verify Console surfaces per-checkpoint metrics and links to traces

rollout_plan:
Gate feature behind runtime flag and gateway annotation; enable for 10% of traffic in staging for 48h
Monitor replay success rate and proxy memory pressure metrics; if stable, increase to 50% then 100% over two weeks
Coordinate client SDK release with server feature gate; older clients should continue to function without service disruption
Add automated rollback if replay errors exceed threshold or if proxy eviction rate climbs above safe limit

comments:
2026-02-19 Asha Patel: Initial draft posted; want feedback from runtime and gateway teams about in-memory buffering limits.
2026-02-24 Marco Ruiz: Prototype encoding implemented in gateway branch; observed 12% memory bump at 100rps with default grace_window=30s. Considering LRU eviction threshold 20MB per worker.
2026-03-02 Priya Sinha (runtime): Confirmed resume endpoint can validate checkpoint id and serve buffered fragments; raised concern about replay load spikes during region failover.
2026-03-10 QA: Added integration tests for function-call atomicity; found edge case where nested tool calls could be split across checkpoint boundaries — fix proposed to require explicit commit before checkpointing.
2026-03-12 Marco Ruiz: Rebased gateway PR, added feature flag and annotation support; beginning staged rollout in staging cluster.
